page.layout: One printed page, numbered at the head. Main text in one column, with marginal notes in the right margin (Quinque loca, Rom. 8. v. 28 area, Chrysostomus). Left margin on the scan belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Verissimum id esse, Inductio docet; commodius, aut minus commodè, explicatium 5. loca, quæ urgemus, præter alia infinita, post Augustinum, & exeo Prosperum Aquit. pro sententia nostra. Videamus autem singula: etsi fortè no adeò id sit necesse. Ipsemet enim Grotius, eis expositis, fatetur: 1. Se neminem iis auctoritatibus premere. 2. homines fuisse: labi potuisse. Quid ergo illi? Urgetis, inquit pro primo loco, Pauli verba, Rom. 8. v. 28. πάντα συνεργεῖ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθὸν τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν. Cur non urgeremus; si de veritate quæstio est? de propósito inquam Dei; & non hominis: cùm ex contextu; tum ex seq. Rom. 9. v. 11? Obstat interpretatio Chrysostomi & Ambrosii. Inquit ille: οὐχ ἡ κλῆσις μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡ πρόθεσις τῶν καλουμένων, τῷ σωτηρίαν εἰργάσατο. ἃ γὰρ ἠναγκασμένη γέγονεν ἡ κλῆσις, ἀδὲ βεβιασμένη. πάντες γὰρ ἐκλήθησαν, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ πάντες ὑπήκουσαν. Nihil hîc de præuisione θεοῦ. Quare libenter damus: 1. Propositionem; Non vocationem solùm, sed & propositum vocatorum, esse operatum salutem. 2. Rationem; Non

page.notes: Marginal notes transcribed: "Quinque loca." (left-hand margin note beside "Quinque loca," in the right margin with "Rom. 8. v. 28." below it) and "Chrysostomus." beside the Greek passage. Greek text is transcribed as best read; accents on the second Chrysostom quotation are uncertain and may contain errors. The final line "Non" is a catchword-like word at the foot of the text and is printed in italic; it is retained in main text. The word "præuisione" and the Greek word after it are partly illegible on the scan; the Greek θεοῦ is a best reading [?]. Some marginal and Greek characters are uncertain throughout.
